newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik peace talks to go ahead despite delay - Russia.
newsitem.headline: Tajik peace talks to go ahead despite delay - Russia.

text.p: Peace talks in Moscow between the Tajik president and the former Soviet republic's armed Islamic opposition are expected to begin on Thursday despite a delay, the Russian Foreign Ministry said.

The discussions, aimed at trying to halt four years of bloody conflict, had initially been scheduled to start in the morning but were postponed until opposition leaders arrived in the Russian capital.

"President (Imomali) Rakhmonov arrived in Moscow on December 18 and the opposition's delegation, headed by Sayid Abdullo Nuri, on December 19," ministry spokesman Mikhail Demurin told a regular news briefing.

He said the two sides were likely to start work later on Thursday but gave no further details. Another Foreign Ministry official told Reuters the two leaders would meet only after their delegations had prepared the documents to be discussed.

RIA news agency quoted a Russian government source as saying Rakhmonov and Nuri would not meet until Friday morning at the earliest. Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov will join the talks, it added.
The foreign ministry's Demurin said: "We are glad that this meeting is taking place and hope it will lead to progress...bringing peace and concord to Tajikistan.
Interfax news agency, quoting a Tajik government official, attributed the postponement of the talks to Nuri's late arrival.
"The Moscow meeting is fundamental," he told Nezavisimaya Gazeta newspaper in an interview published on Thursday.
"First, we should agree on a full ceasefire and an end to other conflict on the border and within the country for the whole period of the negotiating process."
He said a "reconciliation commission" would work on various political issues including reintegrating the exiled opposition.
"I see no option other than a political settlement by peaceful means. In any event, we are ready for this," he added.
He and Nuri are due to discuss the most recent ceasefire agreement in the war-torn republic. Previous deals have been routinely flouted, sometimes immediately after they were signed.

The latest pact was agreed in talks in Afghanistan, but local officials have already reported fighting between government troops and the opposition in the Garm region, some 150 km (100 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe.

In another incident casting doubts on the viability of the latest pact, United Nations military observers monitoring the implementation of the truce were subjected to a mock execution by Tajik government troops, the U.N. mission said on Wednesday.

Opposition sources in Dushanbe said Nuri was delayed in the Iranian capital Tehran for political consultations with other Tajik opposition leaders. Russian media said Moscow was opposed to Nuri's consultations in Iran and had wanted Nuri to fly direct from Afghanistan to Moscow.
